questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
it was crucial for me to have a renowned university as my destination, since I did not want to comprimise the quality of my overall education that I would have otherwise received at UCHP. 

Furthermore, the country was important. One the one hand, southern Europe was appealing. on the other hand, the top quality universities in Germany, Schwitzerland, England and Ireland was very lucrative in the perspective of future career opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The overall quality was 8/10. now, please read the following carefully, please: 

Firstly, when traveling to Ireland and studying in Dublin, you must accept that finding accommodation is REALLY challenging! I would recommend that you start at least 6 months in advance (considering you also have something to attend to in DK, of course. THe reason being that the Irish students will know whether they have been accepted into the universities during the spring/early summer, and they are thus quick to apply for accommodation. the accommodation struggle is famous in Ireland and almost everybody is effected by it. 

Some advice regarding accommodation: 
1) look outside the center of Dublin. Public transport in Dublin is cheap (appx. 20-30 euro/month), and it is usable for the majority of the time. 
2) I personally stayed in the northern part of Dublin (Northwood in Ballymun called "hazelwood"), which was sufficient but only just. I would - in line with the Irish students in general - advice against living in the most nothern parts of Dublin, since this is a troubled area. However, if you live in a gated community, you will be fine (as I did). Other accommodation in the northern part is "Aspen". 

Accommodation can also be found in the center, however the prices of the accommodation will reflect the lucrative location. Personally I paid roughly half as much as those who lived in the center of Dublin. However, you will have to deal with quite a lot of public transport.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Really difficult. We only managed to acquire the information needed by communicating with other students. 

Do not expect Trinity to engage in anything that they are not obliged to, i.e. housing etc. Do not expect Trinity to have sorted out what modules you are enroled in, before you arrive (we did not have ours fully confirmed until 3 weeks into the semester). 

Most of the time you will have to be VERY patient and creative.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any. Trinity was almost completely silent up until the moment when they had to engage with us.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
It was an absolute joke. Nothing was prepared, everything was chaos, i.e.: 
- modules that you applied for and wanted to be enroled in was not taken care of. 
- The classrooms had not been assigned, so neither the professors nor the students knew where to meet for the lectures, 
- the quality of some of the professors and their ability to plan the semester out for the students. 
- the tutors, who were assigned by trinity to act as guidance for the excange students, had not visited the university itself until the very day they met the students that they were supposed to show around (because of COVID).

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: very difficult. see the comments above.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: look for opportunities outside the center of the city. and do make sure to start some months before departing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
See the comments above. the housing market in Dublin - especially for students - is a nightmare (even when compared to other capitals in Europe). 

My best advice is to start early. at least 6 months in advance. most housing agreements can be cancelled if you should decide against going.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Trinity and UCPH use two different systems for registrering courses, it seems. This essentially means that even though the course registration at the UCPH is easy, you will experience that Trinity will make a mess of it, since they are not as advanced as we are in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was non-existing. we had an online zoom-meating where they sort of described something and told us to be patient. law students are lucky in Trinity though, since they are the ONLY students there who can make their module applications online. the rest of the students will apparently have to complete the applications physically on lists in the university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: none. ask the other students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: succesful, in spite of the odds.....

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: i do not think I can give any. Just engage with the other students, and try your best to register. then Im sure you will succeed, too.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: it seemed to be way easier than what we are used to. please do not buy any books over there, you will not need them

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: it was similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EU Competition Law
Administrative Law
IP Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
the same. 

admin law is exceptionally boring at times, but it is funny in the sense that you get to experience how their case law-based law tradition really works, since they do not have any laws or letters of guidance in this area - only caselaw.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: the fitness membership at Trinity. Apparently, they said that UCPH and other universities in Europe does not pay the fee for the sportscenter, so you will have to pay it yourself. However, it is really cheap (app. 75 Euro for a semester).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: food, coffee and beer (especially guiness) was much cheaper than expected. do make sure to go out and enjoy it (8 euros for a pint of guiness IS expensive - aim to get one for 5-6,5 euros).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined the rowing club and used the sports center. the rowing club is fun and great to experience, but they do not want to engage to much with exhange students (though they will hesitate to admit it publicccly), since we are only there for some months.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: all that one could wish for. i joined the kayaking, the fencing club and the rowing club, the sports center and almost the scuba diving club (did not due to a lack of time)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: join the societies! it is great great fun and good ways to meet other people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: all museums etc. that have "national" in their name (i.e. national history museum) are free. These are great for rainy days. other than that go to galway, Howth, Bray, the coastal walks, the old cities and try some of the many restaurants, pubs and cafees. Especially in the beginning of your stay.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: yes, very.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: join the clubs. trinity students are typically not that open to new relationsships (in their own opinion), however they are very friendly when you interact with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: there is some sort of underlying "agression" in some parts of Dublin (typically illustrated by people bumping into you on the streets), whereby the locals are a bit more "rough" than what we are used to in Denmark. also, some fighting can occur on the streets. However, 95% of the time people are friendly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the pub part of the culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Drink Guiness and see the pubs
join a society and do a lot of travelling early on in your stay. 
look for housing and accommodation at least 6 months prior to your stay.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: join the facebook groups for housing in dublin and "danskere i Dublin". they are great.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: living in another country on my own.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the accommodation. by far.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
